extracted.intended_audience: registrants, corporate accountants, and securities lawyers preparing SEC filings for business combinations and joint ventures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on applying SEC/S-X significance tests and the related Rule 3-05/3-01/3-02/3-04/8-02/8-03 financial statement and filing requirements when a registrant acquires or disposes of a business or assets (including joint venture contributions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition significance based on percentage disposed
rubrics_metrics.description: The significance tests for the disposition portion of the transaction are performed in the same way as the acquisition portion, that is based on the percentage of the business disposed, not 100% of the business contributed to the joint venture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a registrant contributes less than 100% (e.g., a 50% interest) to a joint venture, compute the registrant’s share (percentage) of the business contributed/disposed and use that share in the significance tests (investment, asset, income) rather than treating the entire contributed business as disposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment test
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance is measured by the registrant’s share of the fair value of the business/consideration transferred or received divided by the registrant’s AWMV (average market value).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Fair value of business contributed $1,000 × 50% = $500. Registrant AWMV $6,000. Significance = $500 ÷ $6,000 = 8.3%. Apply same calculation for acquisition (consideration transferred) and disposition (consideration received). Compare result to significance thresholds (20%, 40%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset test
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance is measured by the registrant’s share of the carrying value of the assets contributed divided by the registrant’s consolidated total assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Carrying value $750 × 50% = $375. Registrant consolidated total assets $5,000. Significance = $375 ÷ $5,000 = 7.5%. For dispositions, use the carrying value of assets contributed by the registrant and the registrant’s share disposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income test (two components and selection rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: The income test has two components — a pretax income component and a revenue component — each computed as the registrant’s share of the contributed business’s pretax income or revenue divided by the registrant’s consolidated pretax income or consolidated total revenue. The lower of the pretax income component and revenue component is used for the income test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example (acquisition): Pretax component = ($600 × 50%) ÷ $1,000 = 30%. Revenue component = ($1,100 × 50%) ÷ $3,000 = 18.3%. Use the lower result (18.3%) as the income test result. Compare to significance thresholds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance thresholds and consequent financial statement periods (S-X Rule 3-05)
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine required financial statement periods based on whether any significance test condition exceeds set thresholds: none exceed 20%; any exceed 20% but none exceed 40%; any exceed 40%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per S-X Rule 3-05(b)(2): (i) If none of the conditions exceeds 20 percent, financial statements are not required. (ii) If any condition exceeds 20% but none exceed 40%, financial statements must be filed for at least the most recent fiscal year and the most recent interim period specified in §§ 210.3-01 and 210.3-02. (iii) If any condition exceeds 40%, file for at least the two most recent fiscal years and any interim periods specified in §§ 210.3-01 and 210.3-02. Also: if aggregate impact of acquisitions since most recent audited balance sheet exceeds 50% for any condition, additional pro forma and financial statement disclosures are required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate >50% rule (S-X Rule 3-05(b)(2)(iv))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the aggregate impact of businesses acquired or to be acquired since the date of the most recent audited balance sheet exceeds 50% for any condition, the registrant must provide specified pro forma financial information and additional financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required disclosures per (b)(2)(iv): (A) Pro forma financial information pursuant to §§ 210.11-01 through 210.11-02 depicting the aggregate impact; and (B) Financial statements covering at least the most recent fiscal year and the most recent interim period for any acquired or to-be-acquired business for which financials are not yet required by other paragraphs. When evaluating the income test for the >50% aggregation, losses must be aggregated separately from businesses reporting income; if either group exceeds 50%, paragraphs (A) and (B) apply to all specified businesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative significance test for dispositions of assets that are not a business (Form 8‑K Item 2.01 Instruction 4(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the registrant contributes assets that do not meet the definition of a business, the S‑X Rule 1‑02(w) significance tests do not apply; instead, an alternative test applies for determining whether a Form 8‑K must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the alternative test, a disposition of assets (not a business) is significant if either: (a) the registrant’s share in the net book value of the assets disposed of exceeds 10% of the registrant’s consolidated total assets; or (b) the amount received for the assets disposed of exceeds 10% of the registrant’s consolidated total assets. Example: amount received $1,000 × 50% = $500; consolidated assets $4,000; significance = 12.5% → disposition is significant and must be reported on Form 8‑K Item 2.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 3‑01 consolidated balance sheet filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Audited consolidated balance sheets must be filed as of the end of each of the two most recent fiscal years (with specific exceptions and alternative filing date rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key points from S‑X Rule 3‑01: two most recent fiscal years of audited balance sheets generally required; if registrant has existed less than one fiscal year, file an audited balance sheet as of a date within 135 days of filing. For filings made within certain days after fiscal year-end (see (i)), alternative balance sheet timing may apply (additional interim balance sheet requirements). Conditions in paragraph (c) allow use of earlier balance sheets only if specified conditions (timely filing history and income expectations) are met. Timing days differ by filer status: 60/75/90 days and 129/134/135/130 thresholds described for various filers — review rule text for the applicable deadlines and when interim balance sheet inclusion is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 3‑02 statements of comprehensive income and cash flows requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Audited statements of comprehensive income and cash flows must be filed for each of the three fiscal years preceding the date of the most recent audited balance sheet (with limited exceptions for emerging growth companies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: S‑X Rule 3‑02: three fiscal years of audited comprehensive income and cash flow statements are required (an emerging growth company in an initial public offering may supply two years). Interim statements for the period between the latest audited balance sheet and the most recent interim balance sheet must also be provided; these interim statements may be unaudited and condensed per §210.10-01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 3‑04 (changes in stockholders' equity and noncontrolling interests) disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: An analysis of the changes in each caption of stockholders' equity and noncontrolling interests presented in the balance sheets must be provided in a note or separate statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present a reconciliation of beginning balance to ending balance for each period required, with significant reconciling items described by appropriate captions, contributions from and distributions to owners shown separately, and adjustments to beginning balances for retroactive application identified. Provide a separate schedule showing effects of changes in the registrant's ownership interest in a subsidiary on equity attributable to the registrant; state dividends per share and aggregate amounts by class.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 8‑02 annual financial statements for smaller reporting companies
rubrics_metrics.description: Smaller reporting companies must file an audited balance sheet as of the end of each of the most recent two fiscal years (or within 135 days if issuer existed <1 year) and audited statements of comprehensive income, cash flows and changes in stockholders' equity for each of the two fiscal years preceding the date of the most recent audited balance sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule 8‑02 tailors the general S‑X requirements for smaller reporting companies — generally two years of audited income/cash flow/equity statements and two years of balance sheets (with the same shorter‑existence exceptions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 8‑03 interim financial statements and condensed format guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim financial statements may be unaudited; for Form 10‑Q they must be reviewed. Interim statements must include specific balance sheet and income/cash flow items and may be presented in condensed format subject to disclosure thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key Rule 8‑03 points: interim statements may be unaudited but Form 10‑Q interim statements must be reviewed by an independent public accountant (and a report filed if the issuer states that a review occurred). Interim statements must include a balance sheet as of the end of the most recent fiscal quarter, a balance sheet as of the end of the preceding fiscal year, and statements of comprehensive income and cash flows for the interim period and comparable prior period. Condensed format rules: (1) balance sheets should include separate captions for each component presented in annual statements that represents 10% or more of total assets; cash and retained earnings must be presented regardless of relative significance; (2) statements of comprehensive income should include net sales/gross revenue, each cost/expense category that exceeds 20% of sales or gross revenues, provision for income taxes, and discontinued operations. Financial institutions substitute net interest income for sales in determining items to disclose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Periods, age and updating considerations for Rule 3‑05 financial statements in registration and proxy filings
rubrics_metrics.description: Which historical financial statements to provide (number of periods and currency) depends on the filing type, the level of significance, and the timing of the acquisition and the related filing; there are many specific rules about age, updating, relief, and when statements may be omitted or abbreviated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics addressed include: what periods comprise Rule 3‑05 financials; how many periods of financial statements and pro forma information are required depending on significance; meaning of 'age of financial statements'; what annual and interim financial statements are required; when financial statements must be audited under PCAOB standards; pushdown accounting presentation; whether Rule 3‑05 financials can be abbreviated; how the 71‑day Form 8‑K extension affects age; whether previously filed registration statements change Form 8‑K requirements; when Rule 3‑05 financials can be omitted from registration/proxy materials; whether post‑acquisition audited financials can reduce pre‑acquisition audited periods required; relief available when effective or mailing dates fall shortly after fiscal year‑end; S‑X Rule 3‑01(c) conditions affecting required periods; Rule 3‑06 substitution of 9–12 month periods for one year; updating requirements and other timing‑sensitive rules. Practitioners should consult the specific S‑X provisions and the chapter examples for the applicable scenario.
